hero.headline: Gear for the cold end of the season
hero.body: Layering systems, boots, packs and lights for hunters who are still in the timber when the temperature drops and the light runs out. Every piece spends a full season in the field before it earns a place on this page.

grounds.headline: Where are you hunting?
grounds.body: Timber, prairie and marsh ask for different gear. Pick where you'll spend your season and the catalog narrows to what actually works there.

system.headline: Three layers, one kit
system.body: Nobody buys a jacket on its own. Pick one piece from each layer and we price the three together.
system.note: Ships as three pieces, one box. Sizes set at checkout.

lighting.headline: Output you can dial
lighting.body: A 1400-lumen scan drains the cell in four hours. A 200-lumen walk-out runs all night. The Nightfall does both, so you set the beam for the timber you're standing in. Drag the dial.

notes.headline: Eleven jackets and one bad shoulder seam

entries.body: The first Ninebark jackets were sewn in a rented shop off Huffine Lane. There were eleven of them. Eight went to people who hunted with us, and we wore the other three through a full elk season and a late whitetail rut.

Two came back. The shoulder seam on the Ridgeline pulled where a pack strap rides, and the hood wouldn't clear a ball cap. We changed the pattern, moved the seam two inches forward, and put a heavier bar tack at the strap point. That revision is the jacket on this page.
We still cut in Bozeman and we still field-test through a full season before anything gets a price. Nine pieces made it this year. Four didn't, and they'll sit in the back room until they're right.

signature.name: Walt Merrick

newsletter.body: Field notes, restock alerts and the season calendar. Nothing else, and no more than that.
